text:
jess: Ran a profiler on the canary (small traffic) — seeing a host-side CPU bump that lines up with p95 decode latency up ~12%. Early signal points to tokenization + lots of tiny gRPC writes.
marco: link to traces / flamegraph?
jess: Uploaded flamegraph to S3: s3://perf/redwood/canary/6250000000-flame.svg but paste of top lines:
```
  top hot path: tokenize::tokenize_batch (25%)
  grpc::writev_small_chunks (18%)
  parse::http_header_parse (11%)
  kvcache::lookup_miss_path (9%)
```
alyssa: interesting that kvcache shows up too. are we seeing actual eviction spikes or just more misses due to burstiness?
sam: metrics from kvcache: concurrent_streams > 220 -> eviction_rate x2, hit_rate down 8% (canary window).
kevin: so sequence: many concurrent small requests -> tokenizer threadpool gets starved -> more tiny frames -> writev overhead + repeated kv misses because session affinity reshuffles.
marco: any recent changes that could explain tiny write pattern? last release changed http2 windowing/stream-framing defaults (v2.14.3).
jess: yes that change moved default write coalesce window from 4KB -> 1KB for low-latency path. likely culprit for smallwrites.
alyssa: can we try restoring coalesce window and add a parse budget to the tokenizer so it yields earlier? also try increasing tokenizer pool size by +2 for canary.
kevin: alternative: move tokenization to a preparse sidecar thread that accepts batched payloads and returns token spans — then runtime sees larger, fewer writes. downside: more IPC and complexity.
sam: perf-bot ran a quick A/B: canary with +2 tokenizer threads + coalesce=4KB reduced p95 by ~6% and CPU by ~4%. not full fix but promising.
perf-bot: CI profile summary attached: jobs/6250000000/profiles/short.json -> shows writev ops reduced from 12k/s to 3.4k/s on canary variant.
marco: good. can we confirm KV eviction correlation after coalesce bump?
jess: I re-ran kv metrics: after coalesce bump eviction_rate normalized (back to baseline), kv hit_rate went up ~5%. So smallwrites were amplifying concurrent stream churn -> kv thrash.
kevin: kernel-selection note: some backends switch to smaller SIMD kernels for short sequences which ups tokenization cost per-token. if we increase batch size slightly we may nudge kernel selection to a faster path. worth testing with synthetic traces.
alyssa: plan proposal: (1) roll coalesce window back on canary (done), (2) experiment token-pool +2 and parse-yield heuristics (A/B), (3) run synthetic load to exercise kernel-selection thresholds (trace generator: tools/tracegen length distribution), (4) monitor kv eviction + writev rate for 24h.
marco: assign owners?
jess: I'll own tokenizer threadpool experiment and metrics dashboard.
kevin: I'll run kernel-selection synthetic bench and patch heuristics if we see avenue.
alyssa: I'll add a lightweight preparse gated implementation prototype (feature-flagged).
sam: I'll watch kv dashboards and set a regression alert if eviction_rate > baseline * 1.3.
deploy-bot: rolled out canary variant a minute ago to 5% traffic :rocket:
marco: thanks, please ping when canary completes.
jess: initial canary signals already improved, leaving for 6h soak. will post final numbers. :eyes: :thumbsup:
